title: Total internal reflection
examples: What is the critical angle and when do I use it?
How does total internal reflection work in real life?
Can you explain how optical fibres use this principle?

explain.say: Today we are learning about total internal reflection.
First we need to understand what refraction means.

draw.label: Light bends when entering a new material

explain.say: The critical angle is the boundary angle for total internal reflection.
Total internal reflection happens when light goes from dense to less dense.
Optical fibres use total internal reflection to send light signals.
In everyday life, looking into a clear stream shows this principle.

faq.q: What is the difference between reflection and refraction?
faq.a: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one material to another. Reflection is when light bounces off a surface.
asks: Does light just bounce or bend?
What is the difference between bouncing and bending light?

faq.q: Does total internal reflection only happen in water?
faq.a: No, it happens when light moves from a denser medium to a less dense medium. Glass to air is another example.
asks: Can I see this in anything other than water?
What materials can show this effect?

faq.q: What is the critical angle measured in?
faq.a: The critical angle is always measured in degrees. It relates the refractive indices of the two materials.
asks: What units do I use for the critical angle?
Is it measured in meters or degrees?

faq.q: Why are optical fibres so good at sending light?
faq.a: They are designed so that the light stays trapped inside the core using total internal reflection. This keeps the signal strong.
asks: How do they keep the light inside?
What makes optical fibre work so well?

faq.q: If the angle of incidence is small, does reflection happen?
faq.a: Yes, reflection always happens to some degree. Total internal reflection only occurs when the angle is large enough.
asks: Do I need a big angle for reflection?
What angle is needed for total reflection?

facts: Total internal reflection requires light to travel from a denser to a less dense medium.
The critical angle is the specific angle of incidence where the angle of refraction is ninety degrees.
Optical fibres are constructed using materials with different refractive indices.
When total internal reflection occurs, all the light reflects back into the original medium.

quiz.say: Light travels from glass into air. If the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle, what happens?

options.show: The light refracts at ninety degrees.
options.say: The light refracts at ninety degrees.

quiz.why: Because the angle exceeds the critical angle, the light is completely reflected back into the glass.

wrong.1: This would happen if the angle was smaller than the critical angle.
wrong.2: Refraction at ninety degrees only happens exactly at the critical angle.
wrong.3: Scattering is a general term; total internal reflection is a specific, complete reflection.

quiz.say: In an optical fibre, which part has the higher refractive index?

options.show: It depends on the colour of light.
options.say: It depends on the colour of light.

quiz.why: The core must have a higher refractive index than the cladding to trap the light inside.

wrong.0: While colour affects light, the material structure determines the index difference.
wrong.2: If the cladding had a higher index, the light would escape easily.
wrong.3: If they were equal, there would be no difference to trap the light.

quiz.say: A ray of light moves from water to air. If the angle of incidence is exactly the critical angle, what is the angle of refraction?
quiz.why: By definition, at the critical angle, the refracted ray travels along the boundary at ninety degrees.

wrong.0: Zero degrees means the light did not bend at all, which is incorrect.
wrong.1: The angle of refraction is only equal to the angle of incidence in a uniform medium.
wrong.2: The angle is precisely defined as ninety degrees at this specific point.
